title: Bruhat cells and flag charts for a split reductive group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with trivial smooth connected normal unipotent radical. Fix a split maximal torus $T$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with unipotent radical $V$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$, and the right $B$-torsor $\pi:G\to Q=G/B$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $N=|\Phi^+|$ and $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, with action $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n_w^{-1}tn_w)$ on characters. The group $W$ is finite. There is a unique $w_0\in W$ carrying $\Phi^+$ to $-\Phi^+$, and it is an involution. Representatives $n_w\in N_G(T)(F)$ can be chosen for all $w\in W$. For any representative $n_0$ of $w_0$, $B\cap n_0Bn_0^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes. There are smooth locally closed subschemes $C_w\subseteq G$, constituting a disjoint stratification of $G$ compatible with algebraically closed field extensions, and subschemes $V^w\subseteq V$ for which multiplication $V^w\times_F B\to C_w$, $(u,b)\mapsto u n_w b$, is an isomorphism. The longest stratum $C_{w_0}$ is open dense and $V^{w_0}=V$. The map $V\to Q$, $u\mapsto un_0B$, is an isomorphism onto an open dense subscheme $C\subseteq Q$, and $V\simeq\mathbf A_F^N$. The scheme $Q$ has a finite Zariski open cover by translates of $C$, all isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^N$, on each of which $\pi$ has a section and is a trivial right $B$-torsor. Both $G$ and $Q$ are geometrically integral, meaning nonempty, irreducible and reduced after every field extension of $F$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. All isomorphisms and subgroup equalities here are scheme-theoretic, not merely statements about $F$-points.

source.place: Proposition 21.70, Definition 21.72, Theorem 21.73 and Remark 21.74 (pp.446--447); Definition 21.76, Proposition 21.79 and Theorem 21.80 (pp.448--450); Theorem 21.84 and Summary 21.86 (pp.451--452). Geometric integrality and the trivial torsors are the scheme-chart consequences of these statements.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $W$ is finite; each of its cosets has a representative $n_w$. By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit] there is a unique $w_0$ reversing $\Phi^+$ and $w_0^2=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry] to obtain the smooth connected projective scheme $Q$, its equivariant projective embedding, the fixed points $e_w$, and a separating cocharacter $\lambda$ positive on $\Phi^+$. The inverse cocharacter makes $P(-\lambda)$ a Borel with roots $-\Phi^+$ by [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. The Borel $n_0Bn_0^{-1}$ has those same roots. Applying [lem-sfb-unipotent-root-intersection-products] to $B$ and $n_0Bn_0^{-1}$, whose common positive-root set is empty, gives their scheme intersection $T$.

Apply [lem-sfb-projective-attracting-cells] to this projectively linear $\lambda$-action. Its fixed subscheme is precisely the finite reduced set $\{e_w\}$ by the fixed-flag node. Write $Y_w$ for the resulting affine smooth locally closed strata. The tangent-weight list in [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry] gives
$$\dim Y_w=|\Phi^+\setminus w\Phi^+|.$$
The theorem gives both exhaustion of $Q$ and compatibility with algebraically closed extensions. In particular, at $e_{w_0}$ every tangent weight is positive, so $Y_{w_0}$ is open dense.

Use the ordered product coordinates [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and the equivariance in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Conjugation by $\lambda(t)$ multiplies the coordinate of $U_\alpha$ by $t^{\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle}$, a strictly positive power. Thus this conjugation map extends to $t=0$ with constant value $1$. For $u\in V$ and $y\in Y_w$, the identity
$$\lambda(t)(uy)=(\lambda(t)u\lambda(t)^{-1})\lambda(t)y$$
shows the limit remains $e_w$. Hence $Y_w$ is $V$-invariant and contains the orbit $O_w=V e_w$. These statements are scheme-theoretic: the attracting-locus construction is defined by extending orbit maps; equivalently the displayed regular limit calculation is valid over every test algebra.

The stabilizer of $e_w$ in $V$ is $H_w=V\cap n_wBn_w^{-1}$: the torsor identity in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] tests this equality on every algebra. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-root-intersection-products], $H_w$ is smooth with root factors $\Phi^+\cap w\Phi^+$. The root factors of $V$ and $H_w$ are affine lines by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], so [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] gives dimensions $|\Phi^+|$ and $|\Phi^+\cap w\Phi^+|$. The orbit-dimension formula of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] now gives $\dim O_w=|\Phi^+\setminus w\Phi^+|=\dim Y_w$. The orbit is closed in the affine scheme $Y_w$ by [lem-sfb-kostant-rosenlicht-affine-orbits]. A proper closed subset of this affine space has smaller dimension by [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop]. Thus $O_w=Y_w$; both have reduced induced structure. This supplies the missing equality in the printed proof of Milne 21.71 without using Bruhat exhaustion as an assumption.

source.place: 21.71, corrected using 21.77, orbit dimension and 17.64; appended errata p.447.

proof.text: Let $B^-=P(-\lambda)$. Put $V^w=V\cap n_wB^-n_w^{-1}$. The intersection node identifies its root factors as $\Phi^+\cap w(-\Phi^+)$. They complement the root factors of $H_w$. Ordering first those of $V^w$ and then those of $H_w$ in [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] proves multiplication $V^w\times H_w\simeq V$. Right $H_w$-multiplication changes just the second coordinate. The orbit quotient statement [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], applied to $V$ acting on $Q$, therefore identifies $V^w\simeq V/H_w\simeq Y_w$, by $u\mapsto un_wB$. Indeed on the fppf quotient the inverse sends the coset of the unique product $uh$ to $u$, independently of $h$. This is an inverse morphism since the coordinate projection is right $H_w$-invariant. For $w=w_0$ its root set is all of $\Phi^+$, so $V^{w_0}=V$.

Define $C_w=G\times_QY_w$. The torsor identity gives the inverse of multiplication $V^w\times B\to C_w$: for $g$ over a test scheme let $u$ be the unique coordinate of $\pi(g)$ in $Y_w\simeq V^w$; then $b=(un_w)^{-1}g$ is the unique $B$-point given by that identity. Thus $g\mapsto(u,b)$ and $(u,b)\mapsto un_wb$ are inverse scheme morphisms. These are locally closed subschemes because they are inverse images of the $Y_w$, and form a disjoint stratification after every algebraically closed extension. They are smooth: $V^w$ and $B$ are smooth by the intersection and Borel-pair nodes, and products are smooth by base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. For $w_0$, the stratum is the inverse image of the open dense $Y_{w_0}$.

source.place: 21.80(a),(b); explicit trivialization of the pulled-back torsor.

proof.text: Root coordinates and the root parametrizations give $V\simeq\mathbf A_F^N$. The preceding quotient isomorphism identifies $C=Y_{w_0}$ with $V$, with section $u n_0$. Every $F$-point of $Q$ lifts to $G(F)$ by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. Since $C$ contains $e_{w_0}$, its $G(F)$-translates cover all $F$-points of $Q$. Any nonempty complement of their union is closed and has a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]; its residue field is $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], a contradiction. Thus these translates cover $Q$. Properness of $Q$ in the Borel-pair node implies quasi-compactness, so finitely many suffice. On a translate $aC$ the section is $aun_0$, and the torsor isomorphism is $(u,b)\mapsto aun_0b$.

source.place: 21.80(c), or finite translate cover via quasi-compactness; sections from 21.80(b).

proof.text: For every extension $K/F$, $G_K$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and connected by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] (its smooth-connected base-extension clause does not require solvability). It is nonempty by its identity section. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral], $G_K$ is integral. The quotient $Q_K$ is nonempty and irreducible because the torsor projection remains surjective; this follows directly from the finite trivializing cover just constructed, which base changes to $K$ and whose fibres contain $1\in B$. It is reduced since it is covered by the translates of $C_K\simeq\mathbf A_K^N$, whose coordinate rings are polynomial domains: ordering monomials lexicographically, the largest monomial of a product of two nonzero polynomials has the product of the nonzero leading coefficients, so is nonzero. This includes zero variables. Hence $Q_K$ is integral as well. Finally $C_{w_0}$ is a nonempty open of the irreducible $G$, so is dense. This proves geometric integrality and the remaining density assertion, including $\Phi=\varnothing$, when $V=1$, $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$, and the single stratum is $G=B=T$.
